### Unit 5.3A: safe internet usage and passwords

In this unit you will learn how to safely use the internet and at the same time protect your device from malicious software and unauthorised access.

### Top 10 Internet Safety Rules and what not to do Online

Unsafe surfing can also lead to other threats — from embarrassing personal comments or images that, once online, are nearly impossible to erase, to getting mixed up with people you'd rather have had nothing to do with.

Here are the Top 10 Internet safety rules to follow to help you avoid getting into trouble online (and offline).

1. Keep Personal Information Professional and Limited

Potential employers or customers do not need to know your personal relationship status or your home address. They do need to know about your expertise and how to get in touch with you. You would not hand purely personal information out to strangers individually — do not hand it out to millions of people online.

2. Keep Your Privacy Settings On

Marketers love to know all about you, and so do hackers. Both can learn a lot from your browsing and social media usage. But you can take charge of your information. As noted by Lifehacker, both web browsers and mobile operating systems have settings available to protect your privacy online. Major websites like Facebook also have privacy-enhancing settings available. These settings are sometimes (deliberately) hard to find because companies want your personal information for its marketing value. Make sure you have enabled these privacy safeguards and keep them enabled. (http:/lifehacker.com/which-browser-is-better-for-privacy-1525895782) (https:/www.facebook.com/help/325807937506242)

3. Practice Safe Browsing

You would not choose to walk through a dangerous neighbourhood—do not visit dangerous neighbourhoods online. Cybercriminals use lurid content as bait. They know people are sometimes tempted by dubious content and may let their guard down when searching for it. One careless click could expose personal data or infect your device with malware.

4. Make Sure Your Internet Connection is Secure

When you go online in a public place, for example by using a public Wi-Fi connection, you have no direct control over its security. Make sure your device is secure, and when in doubt, wait for a better time (i.e. until you can connect to a secure Wi-Fi network) before providing information such as your bank account number.

5. Be Careful What You Download

A top goal of cybercriminals is to trick you into downloading malware — programs or apps that carry malware or try to steal information. This malware can be disguised as an app: anything from a popular game to something that checks traffic or the weather. Do not download apps that look suspicious or come from a site you do not trust.

6. Choose Strong Passwords

Passwords are one of the biggest weak spots in the whole Internet security structure, but there's currently no way around them. And the problem with passwords is that people tend to choose easy ones to remember (such as "password" and "123456"), which are also easy for cyber thieves to guess. Select strong passwords that are harder for cybercriminals to demystify. Password manager software can help you to manage multiple passwords so that you do not forget them. A strong password is one that is unique and complex — at least 15 characters long, mixing letters, numbers and special characters.

7. Make Online Purchases from Secure Sites

Any time you make a purchase online, you need to provide credit card or bank account information — just what cybercriminals are most eager to get their hands on. Only supply this information to sites that provide secure, encrypted connections. You can identify secure sites by looking for an address that starts with https: (the S stands for secure) rather than simply http: They may also be marked by a padlock icon next to the address bar.

8. Be Careful What You Post

The Internet does not have a delete key. Any comment or image you post online may stay online forever because removing the original (say, from Twitter) does not remove any copies that other people made. There is no way for you to "take back" a remark you wish you had not made or get rid of that embarrassing selfie you took at a party. Do not put anything online that you wouldn't want your mom or a prospective employer to see.

9. Be Careful Who You Meet Online

People you meet online are not always who they claim to be. Indeed, they may not even be real. Be as cautious and sensible in your online social life as you are in your in-person social life.

10. Keep Your Antivirus Program up-to-date

Internet security software cannot protect against every threat, but it will detect and remove most malware — though you should make sure it's to date. Be sure to stay current with your operating system's updates and updates to applications you use. They provide a vital layer of security.

Adapted from:

https://usa.kaspersky.com/resource-center/preemptive-safety/top-10-internet-safety-rules-and-what-not-to-do-online (https:/usa.kaspersky.com/resource-center/preemptive-safety/top-10-internet-safety-rules-and-what-not-to-do-online)

### A strong password is your first line of defence against intruders and imposters.Good practices for creating and using passwords

**Visual 322bdd0184ecec64** (159 × 182 pixels)

Description from visual review: A smiling, waving cartoon computer-mouse mascot introduces or highlights the accompanying teaching note. It contains no task data.

Never give out your password to anyone.

Never give it to friends. A friend can – maybe even accidentally – pass your password along to others or even become an ex-friend and abuse it.

Don’t just use one password.

It’s possible that someone working at a site where you use that password could pass it on or use it to break into your accounts at other sites.

Newest advice: Use a pass phrase.

Security experts are now recommending a “pass phrase” rather than simply a password. Such a phrase should be relatively long – perhaps 20 characters or so and consist of seemingly random words strung together along with numbers, symbols and upper- and lower-case letters. Think of something that you can remember but others couldn’t guess such as YellowChocolate#56CadillacFi$h. that’s relatively long – perhaps 20 characters or so — using seemingly random words strung together along with numbers, symbols and upper- and lower-case letters. Think of something that you can remember but others couldn’t guess such as YellowChocolate#56CadillacFi$h.

Avoid using famous quotations

It might be easy to guess.

Make the password at least 12 characters long.

The longer the better. Longer passwords are harder for thieves to crack.

Include numbers, capital letters and symbols.

Consider using a $ instead of an S or a 1 instead of an L or including an & or % – but note that $1ngle is NOT a good password. Password thieves are onto this. But Mf$J1ravng (short for “My friend Sam Jones is really a very nice guy) is an excellent password.

Don’t post it in plain sight.

This might seem obvious, but studies have found that a lot of people post their password on their monitor with a sticky note. Bad idea. If you must write it down, hide the note somewhere where no one can find it.

Consider using a password manager.

Programs or web services like RoboForm (Windows only) or Lastpass (Windows and Mac) let you create a different very strong password for each of your sites. But you only have to remember the one password to access the program or secure site that stores your passwords for you.

Don’t fall for 'phishing' attacks.

Be very careful before clicking on a link (even if it appears to be from a legitimate site) asking you to log in, change your password or provide any other personal information. It might be a “phishing” scam where the information you enter goes to a hacker. When in doubt, log on manually by typing what you know to be the site’s URL into your browser window.

Make sure your devices are secure.

The best password in the world might not do you any good if someone is looking over your shoulder while you type or if you forget to log out on a cybercafe computer. Malicious software, including “keyboard loggers” that record all your keystrokes, has been used to steal passwords and other information. To increase security, make sure you’re using up-to-date anti-malware software and that your operating system is up-to-date.

Use a 'password' or fingerprints for your phone too.

Most phones can be locked so that the only way to use them is to type in a code, typically a string of numbers or maybe a pattern you draw on the screen. Some new phones allow you to register fingerprints, which are quite secure. Sometimes when people with bad intentions find unlocked phones, they use them to steal the owners’ information, make a lot of calls, or send texts that look like they’re coming from the owner. Someone posing as you could send texts that make it look like you’re bullying or harassing someone in your address book with inappropriate images or words.

Your Password is a secret!

### Multi-Factor Authentication

Another security method some companies use is Multi-factor authentication. With this authentication method a computer user is granted access only after successfully presenting two or more pieces of evidence (or factors) to an authentication mechanism for example:

- knowledge (something the user and only the user knows),

- possession (something the user and only the user has), and

- inherence (something the user and only the user is).

### Two-Factor Authentication

Two-factor authentication uses, as the name implies, two factors to authenticate a user.

An example of two-factor authentication is the withdrawing of money from an ATM.

The correct combination of:

- A bank card (something the user possesses) and a

- PIN (something the user knows)

allows the transaction to be carried out.

Another example is to use a user-controlled password with a one-time password (OTP) or code generated or received by an authenticator (e.g. a security token or smartphone) that only the user possesses.

An online security method some companies use for authentication is CAPTCHA

### Unit 5.3B: Privacy and piracy Acts

In this unit you will learn what is meant by the privacy of information and information piracy.

### Privacy and Security

It is important for young people to know who they can trust with their information especially when they are working online. Security programs and privacy settings can help to block computer viruses and cookies.

You should understand the importance of asking trusted adults to help you to look at a website's privacy policy. You should know the risks associated with creating accounts or downloading files. You must be able to protect yourselves and your digital lives through the knowledge of Internet privacy and safety

| Private | Belonging to one person |
| --- | --- |
| Public | If a fact is made public, it becomes known to everyone rather than being kept secret |
| Privacy | The state of being free from public attention |
| Private information | Is information that can be used on its own or with other information to identify, contact, or locate a single person, or to identify a person |
| Public information | Any information, regardless of form or format, that is disclosed, disseminated, or makes available to the public |

Why should we learn about Information Piracy?

We live in a digital culture that empowers young people to access information instantly, rework media easily, and share their creations globally. But the ease with which young people can find, copy, and distribute digital content can also lead them to use online material without thinking about where it comes from or to whom it belongs. Viewing the Internet as a "free-for-all" leads to problems of copyright infringement, plagiarism, piracy, and a general lack of respect for the hard work and creativity of others. The basic fact is this: Even if something is posted on the Internet for all the world to see, someone somewhere created that picture, song, or article -- and it belongs to that person.

### Unit 5.4: Cybercrime

In this unit you will learn to identify Cybercrime and how to protect yourself against it. We will also have a look at legal implications for someone who makes him/herself guilty of it.

### What is Cybercrime?

Any crimes that involve a computer or digital device and a network is regarded as Cybercrime. Either the computer have been used in order to commit a crime or the computer have been the target of a specific crime.

### Different types of Cybercrime

Take note that you only need to know Identity theft, Phishing and Hacking for assessment purposes.

(Adapted from https://securitytrails.com) (https:/securitytrails.com)

Identity theft

Also known as identity fraud. This is one of the worst crimes that could happen to a person. It starts with the criminal intercepting your personal details like name, identification number, address, cellphone number, and more to impersonate you to commit fraud, steal property or goods, or use services in your name.

A DDos attack (distributed denial-of-service) is a cyber-attack in which the criminal aims to make a computer/digital device or network resource unavailable to its intended users.Botnets

**Visual 322bdd0184ecec64** (159 × 182 pixels)

Description from visual review: A smiling, waving cartoon computer-mouse mascot introduces or highlights the accompanying teaching note. It contains no task data.

The term “botnet” derives from “robot” and “network,” and it is used to refer to a group of controlled computers (bots) that is linked in a network (Internet). These botnets are used to spread malicious files and software, infect other systems, launch DDoS attacks, steal data, send spam and more.

Cyberstalking

Cyberstalking is a form of cyberbullying, where the perpetrator threaten or harass other people by using computer devices connected to the Internet.

Most cyberstalking cases involve the use of anonymous communication systems such as email, social networks, instant messaging applications, etc.; to protect the cyberstalker’s true identity.

Social engineering

Social engineering is a cyber-attack against individuals or organizations where people are manipulated into giving away valuable information. This information can then be used to illegally log into private protected systems or networks to steal for example money, financial data or other sensitive information from a company or customer.

Domain name is the address of a website that people type in the browser URL bar to visit the website.
IP (Internet Protocol) Address is an address of your network hardware. It allows you to connect your computer to other devices on a network. An example of an IP address would be: 506.457.14.512Flood attacks

**Visual 322bdd0184ecec64** (159 × 182 pixels)

Description from visual review: A smiling, waving cartoon computer-mouse mascot introduces or highlights the accompanying teaching note. It contains no task data.

Flood attacks include DoS and DDoS attacks. During these attacks botnets target domain names and IP addresses, to flood systems with malicious requests that overload the servers, leading to service failure and connectivity interruption for legitimate system users.

Potentially unwanted programs

Also known as PUP, refers to software you never officially requested, but has been installed on your system. This type of software usually arrives bundled in other software that you actually have agreed to download and install. Mostly pirated software are the main cause for these attacks. Examples include malicious software like adware, spyware and dialers.

Exploit kits

An exploit kit is a method for delivering malware to an unsuspecting user while that user is surfing the web, without requiring any interaction from that user. Exploit kits use a software toolkit to target vulnerabilities found in remote software. A common example is the act of silently using Flash or Java weaknesses in order to hack a website, then redirecting visitors to malicious pages.

Phishing attacks

Phishing attack is a form of social engineering where users are tricked into providing their login, password, and other sensitive/personal information.

Most phishing operations are executed by sending out spam emails with links to malicious websites that look like legitimate sites for example financial institutions. Once users log into these fake websites, your login details are stored in the attackers’ remote database. They can then use your credit card, bank account or email services for malicious activities.

Illegal content

The Internet is filled with illegal content: this includes all content prohibited by international laws from around the world. Examples of illegal content include pornography, online prostitution services, selling drugs online and copyrighted materials (such as videos, music, books, software, etc.).

Online scams

Online scams (cyber scams) involve fraudulent business offering fake services, goods or rewards to unsuspecting victims. Examples of online scams are charity fraud, gambling fraud, ponzi schemes, online ticket fraud, fake gift cards, automotive fraud and more.

Hacking

Hacking is the activity of using a computer / digital device to access information stored on another computer system without the permission of the user.

### Protection against Cybercrime

- Install reliable, reputable security and anti-virus software.

- Set devices to update automatically. Operating System creators try to issue patches to protect users against cyber-attacks, but can only be applied with the latest security updates.

- Never click on email attachments unless you know the source.

- Delete any social media invitations or messages from people you don’t recognise.

- Buy only software from trustworthy sources, such as the official website for that product; never download or install applications from free sites or advertisements.

- Change passwords regularly, using a unique combination of numbers, letters and case types.

- Install new-generation browsers like Mozilla, Edge, Chrome or Safari, as some older browsers are leaky or no longer supported, and are therefore more vulnerable to attack.

### Legal consequences of Cybercrime

A person convicted of any form of Cybercrime is liable to a fine or imprisonment for a period, depending on the type of crime.

https://www.justice.gov.za/legislation/bills/CyberCrimesBill2017 (https:/www.justice.gov.za/legislation/bills/CyberCrimesBill2017)

#### Unit 6.1 : Introduction To Spreadsheets

In this unit you will learn that a spreadsheet is a type of software for organizing, analyzing, and presenting data in columns and rows. It can also refer to the type of document that you create with this software. It is most useful for dealing with numerical data, and is one of the most frequently used applications in business. You have already worked with a word processor, there are many common features that you will notice in a spreadsheet software.

Common features between a Word Processing Application and a Spreadsheet Application

Both spreadsheet and word processing programs come with utilities that allow you to:

- save your completed files in a variety of formats including as a "Text" and "Rich-Text" files as well as in other formats that are easily processed by other programs.

- carry out spelling and grammar checking, search/replace, as well as

- do page formatting, headers, footers and justification options.

Differences between a Word Processing Application and a Spreadsheet Application

- Word processing programs let you compose a standard letter to send to others with just the other parties details changed using a built-in utility known as a mail merge.

- Word processing programs cannot process formulas directly (without the use of an add-on module), but can accept the result of a calculation.

- Spreadsheet programs cannot process a mail merge, the programs can only provide data for the mail merge.

- Spreadsheet programs use cells, rows and columns to hold data where word processing programs use an open template that doesn't place restrictions on where data can be entered.

| Open Office Calc - is the spreadsheet component of the free opensource Apache OpenOffice software package. |  |

##### Practical Examples Of Spreadsheets Usage

There are various ways spreadsheets are used, here are some uses:

- You can perform calculations using formulas and functions

- You can present your data in graphs

- Excel can be integrated into a other office softwares Word, Powerpoint and Access

- Confidential data can be hidden in a spreadsheet

- You can lock(protect) some data so that people can’t change it

- When you change data in the spreadsheat the results will automatically change if used in other packages, it is called automatic re-calculations, very powerful feature

- You can change the number formating to date, Currency, Time, Text, Accounting

##### Uses Of Spreadsheets

| ### Usage | ### Description | ### Examples |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ### Accounting | Accountants use spreadsheets to help them calculate large sums and analyse data.<br> |  |
| ### sales<br> | Sales teams use spreadsheets to keep track of their customers and follow up on their sales figures<br> |  |
| ### financial management<br> | Money management at all levels starting from a basic family budget to large company budgets are done easily when a spreadsheet software is used.<br> |  |

#### Unit 6.2 : Basic Formatting And Editing

##### Transferring Common Features Knowledge From Word Processing Skills (E.G. Copy, Paste, Save)

After having seen the uses of a spreadsheet software and done some introductory practical activities in our previous lesson. We are now going to continue with practical activities in Excel (A spreadsheet software on the Microsoft Office Suite). We will explore more methods of editing contents of cells.

- Use basic formatting and editing to format cells: wrap, merge, unmerge, alignment, borders, shading, text direction

- Use the autofill feature

When entering data in a cell, you can right click on it, choose format cells where after you can choose what you want to format in the cell or use the shortcut Shift+Ctrl+F.

| Step 1 – Open a blank worksheet and type the word ‘Windmill’ in the cell C3<br>Step 2 – With your mouse pointer on cell C3 right click your mouse and select the ‘Format Cells’ from the drop down menu which will appear.<br>Step 3- Select the alignment tab.<br>Step 4 – Change the text orientation to 45 degrees by either moving the dial till it reaches 45 or just typing 45 in the degrees spin button.<br>Step 5 – Press the ‘OK’ button to accept the changes you have done.<br> |  |
| #### Guided Activity 2: Adding different kinds of shading effects (continuation from GA 2) |  |
| Step 1 – Right Click cell C3 and select ‘Format Cells’, then the ‘Fill’ tab<br>Step 2 – Click on the ‘Fill Effects’ button for the fill effects window to appear.<br>Step 3 – Leave the ‘Colors’ as 2 and select the ‘Diagonal Up’ Shading Style, choose the ‘Variant’ with the darker centre.<br>Step 4 – Click the OK button to accept the changes, and OK again to effect view the changes.<br> |  |
| #### Guided Activity 3: Changing putting a background pattern of cells and putting a border |  |
| Step 1 – Type the word ‘Windmill Computers’ in cell D4, font name= Impact, font size= 32<br>Step 2 – Double Click on the right side of the cell header to resize the cell to fit the text, then highlight the cell, right click your mouse and select ‘Format Cells’<br>Step 3 – In the ‘Fill’ tab select the ‘Pattern’ drop down menu to choose pattern of your choice<br>Step 4 – Click on the pattern of choice and then click the ‘OK’ button to effect and view the changes<br> |  |

#### Unit 6.3 : Basic Data Types And Formulae

##### Common data types

A spreadsheet programme will need to know the format of the data that is being used. The datatypes that are commonly used in many spreadsheets are:

  - General – a datatype that has no specific data format

  - Number, including number of decimal places – you can only use numbers

  - Currency, including number of decimal places – used to represent money values

  - Text – used to represent text, even if you enter a number it will be considered as text.

Before entering data into a spreadsheet, you must be must know what you want to accomplish with that data. Generally there are two main actions that you can do on with data, either you want to use it for calculation (number or currency) or you want to use it to describe numbers(text).

We are not used to performing mathematical operations(+, -, *, /) with text but as you get more and more comfortable with Excel, you will realise that nothing is impossible.

### WHY is it important to use cell references rather than constant values in cells and formulas:

Why use A1 and not 100

When using a formula for example =(A1+A1) the value (100) change to 200

When using a formula =(100+100) the answer will be 200 as well

BUT: If you change the value (100) to 120, the formula used in the third bullet will not change.

Basic maths calculations using

  - + (plus)

  - –

  - *

  - /

There is a difference between the (x) in maths and (*) in excel, and also (÷) in maths and (/) in excel.

Order of precedence and brackets

  - The formulas in a spreadsheet are in the same order as in Mathematics precedence.

  - First Brackets

  - Second Powers and Square roots

  - Third Division and Multiplication from left to right

  - Last Addition and subtraction from left to right

##### Functions

### We Use Basic Functions: Min, Max, Sum, Count And Average To Solve Simple Problems

- Formulas are calculations that you can create (like a calculator) in order to get an answer

- EXAMPLE = (30/3)+2+4*10

- Functions are calculations that are already made and stored into Excel.

- EXAMPLE = sum(cell reference1:cell reference2)

or

= sum(cell Range)

### Unit 6.6 : Error Indicators And Troubleshooting

##### basic errors and indicators

### common errors and solutions

Spreadsheets help you by giving out an error if there are problems with the spreadsheet. We are now going to identify problems based on the following error indicators: #VALUE, #NAME, #NUM, #REF, #DIV/0, #N/A, ######

- ##########

| Reason | Solution |
| --- | --- |
| The column is not wide enough to display answer | Widen the column by draging it bigger |

- #NAME!

| Reason | Solution |
| --- | --- |
| Typing/Spelling misktake | Check the spelling of function names |

  - #REF!

| Reason | Solution |
| --- | --- |
| The cell reference in the formula is not valid anymore, maybe that cell, row, column is been deleted | Change cell reference to the correct cell. |

- #DIV/0!,

| Reason | Solution |
| --- | --- |
| Division by zero, this happens when you try to devide by zero or maybe an empty cell | Check your cell, if its empty type in the corect value |

- #VALUE!

| Reason | Solution |
| --- | --- |
| Incorrect data used, for instance where text is multiplied by a number | Check your cells, make sure there is no text in it. Maybe you typed in the R for R10.99 |

- #NUM!

| Reason | Solution |
| --- | --- |
| Incorrect data used, for instance where text is multiplied by a number | Check your cells, make sure there is no text in it. Maybe you typed in the R for R10.99 |

##### Troubleshooting

When a possible solution done using Excel does not yield the desired outcome, there may be countless reasons. Some of the problems may need complex solutions while others may need fixing simple things. In both cases a scientific and systematic way, composed of basic steps are taken to troubleshoot the problem, in order to find the error.

### Here Are The Four Common Steps Used In Solving Common Software Issues

Identify the symptom:

- Identify the Type of Issue.

- Find the problem area.

- Note relevant configuration information.

Eliminate non-issues:

- Make sure the correct patches, drivers, and operating systems are installed.

- Try earlier releases (back-tracing).

- Minimize the test. Restrict the test to as few issues at a time as possible.

- Minimize the hardware and software configuration. Determine if the problem is reproducible on single and multiple systems. Determine if the problem changes with the browser version.

- Determine if the problem depends on whether multiple VMs are installed.

Find the cause:

- Check for typical causes in the area.

- Use flags to change defaults.

- Use tracing.

Find the fix:

- Find a possible workaround.

- File a bug.

For guidance on how to submit a bug report and suggestions on what data to collect for the report, see Submit a Bug Report.

- Fix the setup.

- Fix the application.

### Definitions

| - A spreadsheet is an electronic document in which data is arranged in the rows and columns of a grid and can be manipulated and used in calculations.<br><br>- A row is the range of cells that go across (horizontal) the spreadsheet/worksheet. Rows are identified by numbers e.g. row 1, row 5. Examples of use. A row might contain the headings of a table e.g. product ID, product name, price, number sold.<br><br>- Define a column as as the range of cells that go down/up (vertically) the spreadsheet/worksheet. Columns are identified by alphabetical letters e.g. column A, column AC.<br><br>- Define a cell as the intersection between a column and a row. A cell can contain text or numbers and can be identified by the letter of the column combined by the number of the row.<br><br><br><br><br> |

At the end of this chapter you should be able to do the following in Scratch:

- Create a project

- Understand the Scratch environment

- Use various basic coding blocks

- Create animations using coding blocks

- Code a project using simple decision making

- Code a project using simple repetition

- Draw different shapes applying computational thinking

### Term 4Unit 7.1: introduction to coding

### Introduction

An easy way to start your coding/programming experience is by using a block-based programming language like Scratch. A block-based programming language enables you to create your own interactive stories, animations and games.

In a block-based coding environment you are given commands, called blocks, that you only need to drag-and-drop in an appropriate fashion to code your project.

Scratch is available free of charge from the following website https://Scratch.mit.edu. The activities following this unit is written for Scratch version 3. (https:/scratch.mit.edu)

### The Scratch Environment

### Guided Activity 7.1.1

In this activity you will learn to code your first project. Most computer languages start off with a “Hello World program.” We are not changing this tradition.

2. The Scratch environment includes the following:

| The Sprite, also called an Actor/Object (software agent) | The Sprite is an object you will find on the Stage Area. The default Sprite is the Cat you see. The Sprite can have certain looks and perform certain action according to the coding blocks given. |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The Sprite Selection area | The Sprite Selection Area is where you can:<br>- add different Sprites to the Stage.<br>- change the name of the Sprite.<br>- show/hide the Sprite.<br>- change the size and direction of the Sprite.<br>- see the coordinates of the Sprite. |  |
| The Choose a Sprite icon | The Choose a Sprite Icon is where you can:<br>- choose another Sprite.<br>- paint your own Sprite.<br>- Get a Surprise Sprite – it chooses a random Sprite from all Sprites that are available on Scratch.<br>- load your own Sprite. |  |
| The Choose a Backdrop icon | The Choose a Backdrop Icon is where you can:<br>- choose another Backdrop.<br>- paint your own Backdrop.<br>- Get a Surprise Backdrop – it chooses a random Backdrop from all Backdrops that are available on Scratch.<br>- load your own Backdrop. |  |
| The Script area | The Script Area is found in the centre of the screen. This is where you will code a Script by dragging different coding blocks from the Block Palette.<br>A Script is a set of coding blocks that gives the Sprite/Actor/Object and/or Backdrops instructions to perform. |  |
| The Stage | On the right of the screen is the Stage. All coding blocks are acted out/performed here by the Sprite/actor/object and/or Backdrop according to the Script. |  |
| Block Palette | Coding blocks are classified according to categories in the Block Palette:<br>- Motion Blocks are coding blocks that can move or glide the Sprite/Actor/Object and turn the Sprite/Actor/Object any direction. These coding blocks are dark blue. You can only use Motion Blocks with Sprites/Actors/Objects, not with the Stage.<br>- Looks Blocks are coloured purple, and they control what your Sprites/Actors/Objects and Backdrop look like, how big they are, and whether they are displayed in front of or behind other assets. Looks Blocks also include coding blocks that let you display text.<br>- The next set of blocks is the pink Sound Blocks. These coding blocks are to add sound.<br>- The brown Events Blocks are fundamental to Scratch, without them, nothing will happen. Each Script (set of commands) will have an event at its start which tells the Script (set of commands) to run. This might be the Green Flag being clicked to start, or it might be an Event that is triggered while your project is running.<br>- Control Blocks (in orange) let you control the coding blocks within your Scripts, inserting Conditional Statements, Loops, Repeats and Pauses.<br>- Sensing Blocks are coloured light blue. They let you identify what's happening at a given point and make your Sprites/Actors/Objects or Backdrop respond.<br>- Operator Blocks (in pink) let you make comparisons between or perform arithmetic functions on different values<br>- Variables Blocks let you define values for a variable and then use it in your project. They're great for timing games or keeping score, or for defining how many times a Loop needs to run Lists can be used to store and manipulate grouped or related data.<br>- Use the dark purple 'more' Block option to create your own coding blocks. | <br><br> |

### Unit 7.2: Simple Decision Making

### Introduction

In the previous unit you learned how to code your first program “Hello World.”

In this unit you will learn about simple decision making based on a specific condition.

### Simple IF-THEN Statement

A program is often given options and must then decide which instructions to follow by evaluating the condition(s). For example, when you walk out the door, you look at the weather and based on whether it looks as if it is going to rain, you may decide to take your ambarella or not. The weather condition influences your decision and your action(s) based on this decision. So, you will ask yourself: Is it going to rain? The answer will be Yes or No. Based on the answer, you will act accordingly.

IF it rains, THEN take your umbrella.

The same happens in programming. The decision structure (IF-THEN statement) allows a program to evaluate a condition, then based on the outcome of that, execute certain instructions.

You will find the simple IF-THEN statement block in the Control Block section.

- A condition always returns one of two answers: Yes or No. This is the same as True (yes) or False (no), e.g. The statement, ”It is raining” can either be True or False.

- In the simple IF-THEN statement, when the condition is TRUE, the coding blocks inside the IF-THEN block will followed (executed).

- If the condition results in a FALSE, the coding blocks inside the IF-THEN block will be skipped and the first instruction (coding block), outside the IF-THEN block will be performed (executed).

### Guided Activity 7.2.1

Start

- Set the music instrument to organ

- Think “I will play an instrument”

- Wait for 1 second

- If the key 1 (one) is pressed:

  - Say “Happy Birthday to you”

  - The first part of the song “Happy Birthday” is played

- If the key 2 (two) is pressed

  - Say “I cannot play an instrument”

### Unit 7.3: Animation in Scratch

### Introduction

In the previous unit you learned how to use the simple IF-THEN-statemen to make a decision.

In this unit you will learn to repeat instructions in Scratch.

Before you learn about repetition (repeating instructions) in Scratch, you need to understand what sequencing is.

### Sequencing

You already learned about “sequencing” in Chapter 4. Sequencing is putting events or information or instructions in a specific order. It is the skill that helps you to plan what steps to take in which order to perform a task successfully.

In coding it is very important to write commands in the correct logical order. For instance, if you start counting you will count 1..2..3..4, etc. In coding, instructions follow each other, and they must follow each other in a logical manner. For example, have you thought what will happen if you move the “play note” coding blocks in the previous example, around? If the coding blocks are not sequenced correctly (not in a logical order), the song will not sound right anymore. Sequencing is very important concept in coding.

### FOREVER loop

Sometimes, in coding, you want code/commands to repeat an infinite time. In Scratch structure that we use to have something repeated for an infinite time, is the FOREVER loop.

You will find the FOREVER block in the Control Block section.

The FOREVER block looks like this:

### Unit 7.4: Limited Repetition

### Introduction

In the previous unit you learned how to create an animation using the FOREVER Loop.

In this section we will write a Script (set of commands) that will repeat coding blocks for a specific number of times.

### The Counting repeat

With the FOREVER Loop the coding blocks will perform an infinite time. With the Counting Repeat you can code the Sprite/Actor/Object how many times the coding blocks must be repeated.

The simple Counting Repeat block you will also find in the Control Block. The block looks like this:

### UNIT 7.5: Drawing Shapes

### Introduction

In the previous units you learned about decision making and repetition and in Chapter 4 you learned about using computational thinking and how that helps to see patterns that could help you draw shapes.

You are now going to use what you learned about patterns, drawing shapes and repetition to draw shapes in Scratch.

How will he do it?

Quickly reflect on what you learned about computational thinking. What are the four computational thinking corner stones or techniques? Oh yes!

- Abstraction,

- Decomposition,

- Pattern recognition, and

- Algorithms.

| Technique 1: Abstraction<br> | Focusing on the important details and ignoring the things you do not need. | We have seen this before – it is a square. In Mathematics we also learned about squares. |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Technique 2: Decomposition<br> | Breaking a difficult problem into small manageable parts | The square has 4 sides and 4 angles<br>If we draw each line at a time, we can solve the problem easier. |
| Technique 3: Pattern Recognition | Recognition the same patterns in other problems to help you in solving a particular problem. | Ahh! All 4 sides are the same lenngth and all 4 angles are the size. |
| Techniques 4: Algorithm | A set of rules or steps that anyone can follow to solve a problem. | - Draw a straight line: 100 steps<br>- Turn 90 degrees right<br>- Draw a straight line: 100 steps<br>- Turn 90 degrees right<br>- Draw a straight line: 100 steps<br>- Turn 90 degrees right<br>- Draw a straight line: 100 steps<br>- Turn 90 degrees right |

An algorithm is a set of logically sequenced. These instructions can be translated into computer code (called a programming language). You have already use algorithms and translated it into Scratch code or commands.

Another type of coding, that is possible without a computer (called unplugged computing), is Puzzle-based coding. Puzzle based coding such as used in “Scotty”, “Tanks”, and “Ranger” use the same algorithm makes use of physical puzzle pieces to build the lines of code (set of commands). With the use of a mobile phone application, the code can be executed. For now, we are only going to read and interpret the code and follow the instructions with pen-on-paper.

| --- | --- | --- |

### TemplatesStorage.docx

Source: `5. LEARNER GUIDE/Grade 8/Datafiles/Chapter 1 Systems Technology Data/Ch1Files/TemplatesStorage.docx`

Telling Word 2019 where templates are stored

The first time you create a template, Word stores it in this folder:

- C:\Users\Username\Documents\Custom Office Templates

However, in previous versions of Word, templates were stored in one of these folders:

- C:\Users\Owner\Documents\Custom Office Templates

- C:\Users\Username\AppData\Roaming\Microsoft\Templates

To keep all your templates in one place, either move them to the C:\Users\Username\Documents\Custom Office Templates folder or tell Word where you prefer to store templates.

Follow these steps to tell Word 2019 where you keep templates on your computer:

1. On the File tab, choose Options.
The Word Options dialog box opens.

2. Go to the Save category.

3. In the Default Personal Templates Location text box, enter the path to the folder where you prefer to store templates.

4. Click OK.

### Activity 2_7.docx

Source: `5. LEARNER GUIDE/Grade 8/Datafiles/Chapter 2 Keyboarding Data Files/Activity 2_7.docx`

Video provides a powerful way to help you prove your point. When you click Online Video, you can paste in the embed code for the video you want to add. You can also type a keyword to search online for the video that best fits your document.

To make your document look professionally produced, Word provides header, footer, cover page, and text box designs that complement each other. For example, you can add a matching cover page, header, and sidebar. Click Insert and then choose the elements you want from the different galleries.

Themes and styles also help keep your document coordinated. When you click Design and choose a new Theme, the pictures, charts, and SmartArt graphics change to match your new theme. When you apply styles, your headings change to match the new theme.

Save time in Word with new buttons that show up where you need them. To change the way a picture fits in your document, click it and a button for layout options appears next to it. When you work on a table, click where you want to add a row or a column, and then click the plus sign.

Reading is easier, too, in the new Reading view. You can collapse parts of the document and focus on the text you want. If you need to stop reading before you reach the end, Word remembers where you left off - even on another device.

### Activity 3.5.2.docx

Source: `5. LEARNER GUIDE/Grade 8/Datafiles/Chapter 3 Word Data Files/Activity 3.5.2.docx`

Pemberly Furniture and Interiors

Getting the Look you want

If you are intimidated by the prospect of decorating your home, you definitely are not alone. The endless choices available to today’s consumer can be overwhelming. To help you get the look you want, the designer s at PFI made the following suggestions.

### Ask Yourself Some Questions

Think about places you’ve been where you felt especially comfortable recently – a friend’s house, for instance, or a stylish restaurant. How did those places make you feel? What did you like about them? Ask yourself the following questions about each place:

What was the colour scheme?

Was the room cluttered or bare?

Was the furniture made of wood or metal, or was it upholstered?

Would you describe the room as formal or casual?

For the next weeks, continue to analyse your surroundings whenever you visit a new place. Then, with this new awareness of your likes and dislikes, make a list of elements you want to incorporate into your own home. It’s also helpful to make a list of elements you want to avoid.

### Pick a style

Now that you know what you like and don’t like, you are ready to identify the style that suits your taste. Having an official name for your style will help sales people zero in on the products that will work best for you. People who are seriously interested in interior decorating make fine distinctions between styles. French country, cottage style, vintage retro, and Victorian are only some of the many possibilities. However, if your goal is simply to give your house a pleasant, coherent look, there’s no need to go into such detail. Most likely, your tastes fall into one of four basic styles:

Formal

Traditional

Eclectic

Contemporary

Stay true to your style

People who enjoy spending time thinking about and decorating their homes will often mix-and-match furniture and accessories from thesefour basic styles. You can pick a style for your house and stick with it. Note that you probably will want to combine styles within your house (for example, a formal living room and a casual family room). Within an individual room, however, a single style is the surest way to create a pleasing interior.

Of course, you probably won’t be able to redo every room in your house from top to bottom according to your chosen styles. For most people, decorating a home involves a series of purchases and improvement over time.

To maximize your design statement, consider making your purchases in the following order:

Large items such as sofas, beds, and dining tables

Lamps or other accent pieces

End tables and other accent pieces

Rugs or other floor coverings

While you are saving money to complete the look of a particular room, purchase smaller items (vases, mirrors, or picture frames) that can accentuate a room’s style without breaking your budget.

These are just some ideas to help you get started. To learn more about decorating your home, consider scheduling a consultation with Natalie Lanci, or one of are other fine designers at PFI

### Article on Spekboom.docx

Source: `5. LEARNER GUIDE/Grade 8/Datafiles/Chapter 3 Word Data Files/Article on Spekboom.docx`

Portulacaria afra

Portulacaria afra (known as elephant bush, dwarf jade plant, porkbush and spekboom in Afrikaans) is a small-leaved succulent plant found in South Africa. These succulents commonly have a reddish stem and leaves that are green, but also a variegated cultivar is often seen in cultivation. They are simple to care for and make easy houseplants for a sunny location. In frost-free regions they may be used in outdoor landscaping. (https:/en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afrikaans) (https:/en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Succulent_plant) (https:/en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Africa)

Description

It is a soft-wooded, semi-evergreen upright shrub or small tree, usually 2.5–4.5 metres (8–15 ft) tall. Similar in appearance to the unrelated "jade plant" Crassula ovata (family Crassulaceae), P. afra has smaller and rounder pads and more compact growth (shorter internodal spaces, down to 1.5 mm). It is much hardier, faster growing, more loosely branched, and has more limber tapering branches than Crassula once established.[1] (https:/en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crassula_ovata) (https:/en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crassulaceae) (https:/en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portulacaria_afra)

The genus Portulacaria has been shown to be an outlier, relatively unrelated to the other genera in the family, which are all restricted to small ranges in the arid far west of Southern Africa. (https:/en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portulacaria) (https:/en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Africa)

Distribution and habitat

It is very widespread in the east of South Africa (including Eswatini). In this moist climate, it is relatively rare, and tends to favour dryer rocky outcrops and slopes. (https:/en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Africa) (https:/en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eswatini)

It is also found in much denser numbers in the dryer southern Cape. Here it occurs from the Little Karoo of the Western Cape, eastwards up until the thicket vegetation of the Eastern Cape. Spekboom is found most prolifically in the Albany thickets, a woodland ecoregion, which locally is often called noorsveld, after the high number of succulent Euphorbia species, which are often called noors plants. (https:/en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Little_Karoo) (https:/en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Cape) (https:/en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thicket) (https:/en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Cape) (https:/en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albany_thickets) (https:/en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecoregion) (https:/en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euphorbia)

Cultivation and uses

"Prostrata" decumbent variety

In the wilds of South Africa, large plants do survive the winter frosts by growing dense enough to provide their own natural cover. Drought-tolerant and fire-resistant, it will endure desert sun and heat once established, which the jade plant will not. Portulacaria is a common landscape plant in Phoenix, Arizona. Cuttings root very easily in most potting media. (https:/en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuttings_(plant))

### Respect the Spekboom.docx

Source: `5. LEARNER GUIDE/Grade 8/Datafiles/Chapter 3 Word Data Files/Respect the Spekboom.docx`

Respect the spekboom!

JULY 31ST, 2017

Portulacaria afra, commonly known as spekboom, is a drought-resistant, indigenous succulent native to our country. Although mainly an inhabitant of the Little Karoo and Eastern Cape, it also grows in dry river valleys in the east and up to the Limpopo, and on the slopes of the Soutpansberg. In late winter you may be lucky to see them covered in pink flowers. Here at Babylonstoren we have a nice spread of spekboom adjacent to the three fish ponds.

Huh? Spekboom eats my car’s carbon dioxide?

The spekboom earns enormous value for its carbon credits, and is highly regarded in terms of the voluntary carbon standard mechanism, making this humble oukie a red carpet rave on the international market. Although all plants trap carbon dioxide from the air to photosynthesize and grow, spekboom is highly efficient at this because it can still trap carbon dioxide even if its breathing pores are closed. (https:/en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Voluntary_Carbon_Standard)

Here’s how it works: Spekboom has the ability to change its photosynthesis pathway depending on rainfall and temperature. When conditions are favourable, it trots the same pathway as other plants (C3 photosynthesis). However, during harshly dry conditions, it switches to a different type of photosynthesis called CAM (Crassulacean Acid Metabolism). Now the plant closes the pores (or stoma) in its leaves and branches during the day so that no unnecessary transpiration takes place. Yet it remains able to photosynthesise. This is made possible by acid that builds up in the leaves during the night (stored as carbon dioxide), and is broken down during the day. In this way our friend efficiently captures large amounts of carbon using very little water.

### Spekboom salad.docx

Spekboom, Chickpea And Tomato Salad

by Jacques Erasmus for Woolworths Taste

Ingredients

2 x 400 g cans chickpeas, drained and rinsed

250 g baby tomatoes

2 avocados, peeled, pitted and sliced

1/2 onion, sliced and blanched

two handfuls spekboom leaves, rinsed

Maldon salt, to taste

For the dressing, mix together

1/3 cup extra virgin olive oil

3 T white-wine vinegar

1 T honey

1 T smooth mustard

freshly ground black pepper

2 sprigs flat-leaf parsley, roughly chopped

Method

Remove the chickpea shells and place in a salad bowl with the tomato, avocado, onion and Spekboom leaves and pour over the dressing. Lightly mix and allow to rest for 2 to 3 minutes before serving, sprinkled with salt, to taste.

### Spekboom.docx

Source: `5. LEARNER GUIDE/Grade 8/Datafiles/Chapter 3 Word Data Files/Spekboom.docx`

boldStyles: Intense Quote21 MARCH 2019 | PUBLISHED BY ADMIN

Styles: Book TitleSpekboom (Portulacaria Afra) is a succulent plant found in South Africa. It is indigenous to the Eastern Cape province and has been deemed as a miracle plant by many. It is a bright green, small-leaved plant with a contrasting red stem found in Southern Africa that seems ordinary but don’t be fooled – it is a very special plant!

Interesting Facts About the Spekboom Plant & Its Uses

italicunderlineThe spekboom plant is a sprawling shrub or small tree; occurring in karroid (semi desert) areas and bushveld. It is usually found in rocky places and grows prolifically in parts of the Eastern Cape. The leaves are circular and bright green or pale grey. The plant has a glossy red-brown trunk and bears a dense crown of succulent leaves and stems.

Styles: Subtle EmphasisIt is most attractive in full bloom as a mass of soft pink nectar-rich flowers flourish at the ends of the branchlets. After flowering, tiny papery three-winged fruits populate the unassuming spekboom plant. This versatile plant has several uses:

#1 Leaves are Edible

The taste of spekboom leaves are pleasant but changes throughout as the sun rises and sets. During the day leaves have an acid flavour and they become less acidic towards the evening. The delicious greenery is heavily browsed by game and firm favourite of several wild animals, especially elephants!

#2 Communities Use Spekboom Leaves for Their Medicinal Values

The leaves are used medicinally and in traditional home construction. In certain areas, the stems are used to help build huts/homes. The stems are dried and used as thatch for rooves of the huts/homes. The spekboom flowers are nectar-rich and provide food for many insects – endangered bees love them! This, in turn, attract insectivorous birds. Larvae of the Duadem butterfly also feed on the Portulacaria species.

### The History of animation.docx

Source: `5. LEARNER GUIDE/Grade 8/Datafiles/Chapter 3 Word Data Files/The History of animation.docx`

The History of animation
Animation is the capturing of sequential, static images—drawings or photos of inanimate objects—and playing them in rapid succession to mimic real world motion. If you’ve ever seen a flip book, you know how it works.

But chances are, when you ask “what is animation?” you want something more than a technical definition. Where did it come from? What’s the appeal?

Although the idea of sequential art dates back thousands of years—more, depending on your interpretation of cave paintings—animation as we know it was only made possible by the invention of the film strip. However, the optics behind animation has been known since the early 1800s, as we see from Simon von Stampfer’s phénakisticope(1833) below.

On of the first animation on film was actually hand-painted by the French artist and inventor Charles-Emile Reynaud on his Praxinoscope—one of the stepping-stone inventions that led to the film camera.

For the first part of the 1900s, artists from all over the world experimented with animation, such as the recently discovered Katsudō Shashin, dated from 1907 to 1911 and said to predate much of Western animation. However, animation was thought of mostly as a novelty until the era of Walt Disney in the 1920s, when sound was beginning to be implemented in movies. Steamboat Willie (1928), Disney’s “flagship” cartoon, was not the first cartoon with sound, but it was one of the most popular at the time. (https:/en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katsud%C5%8D_Shashin)

By the 1930s, other studios caught on that there was money to be made through animation, the impetus behind Warner Bros. launching Looney Tunes and Merrie Melodies. The 1930s saw friendly rivalry between Mickey and Bugs — known now as the American Golden Age of Animation — which culminated in a Disney’s power play Snow White and the Seven Dwarves, the first feature-length film to be made entirely of hand-drawn images.

The rest is history. With the popularization of color TV in the late 1950s, another American animation pioneer Hanna-Barbera entered the scene. Following the 1960s cultural revolution, animation was co-opted for adults, most famously the X-rated Fritz the Cat (1972) based on the work of legendary comic artist Robert Crumb. Finally, in the 1990s, computer generated imagery (CGI) was able to compete with hand-drawn animation, popularized by the first completely-CGI film Toy Story (1995).

Considering the wide-ranging history of animation, we see its appeal is wide-ranging as well. Kids love it, of course, because most of the stories for children involve talking animals, tea kettles, or visuals otherwise impossible to bring to life.

But the more sophisticated the animations techniques become, so too do the themes they discuss. While CGI is used in almost every movie today, even completely animated features can appeal to adults—just look at popular animated sitcoms like The Simpsons, Family Guy or South Park.

Perhaps the greatest strength isn’t that it appeals to different groups, but all groups at once. Animation allows artists to invoke that childlike wonder and awe of not believing our eyes, but to harness that power for more mature storytelling and even business, as we explain below.

How can this visual technique appeal to both our inner child and our discerning adult at the same time? Just look at practically any Pixar movie. This is a safe space—are you going to tell me you didn’t get misty-eyed during the first ten minutes of Up?

### What is animation.docx

Source: `5. LEARNER GUIDE/Grade 8/Datafiles/Chapter 3 Word Data Files/What is animation.docx`

What is animation: a guide to its history and modern use in design?

There was a point in everyone’s life when animation was just the coolest thing you’d ever seen. Whether it was a Disney movie as a kid or maybe a 3D game cut scene that blew you away, there was always something spectacular when imaginary characters move and act as in real life.

And don’t think that power went unnoticed by graphic designers.

In the digital era, animation can do more than just entertain children with a boat-driving mouse. It’s an effective tool for visual communication. Of course, it offers a whole new medium for expression and creativity, but on a more practical level, the movement of animation attracts more attention than static images. And considering the restraints of live footage, sometimes an animation of a bouncing ball works best.

In this article, we give an all-encompassing animation overview. We discuss animation for designers and give some techniques from the heyday of cartoons a much-needed update for the modern era. We also showcase the business side of animation, explaining how it can improve both the UX of your website and the effectiveness of digital marketing campaigns. So without further ado, let’s get moving!

### Sports_Day_Gr8.docx

Source: `5. LEARNER GUIDE/Grade 8/Datafiles/Practical Project/Question 1/Sports_Day_Gr8.docx`

Sports Day Activities for Secondary School

Sports dy is the highlight of the school year for lots of pupils and teachers, so you want to make it an event to remember with lots of activities to enjoy. There are a few things to consider when planning a secondary school sports dy; there are usually far more children in Secondary school than in Primary, and there's a great age difference. Some schools plan to have 2 sports dys, 1 for Years 7-9 and the other for Years 10-11, whilst others choose to wait until after the Year 11 pupils have left the school in the summer term and host a whole school event.

Who's Involved?

Is it best to involve everyone, from children to parents, or keep it as a school-only affair?

For Primary schools, the school sports dy is usually the highlight of the summer for parents as well as the kids, so the parents love to be involved and join in as much as possible. They're quite happy to join in the races and help on the dy.

Once the children move to Secondary school, the kids are quite happy to take part and help with arranging the events independently of their parents, so many Secondary schools host the event during school hours just for the children.

Choosing the Events

Do you choose some elements of the Primary games such Egg and Spoon races and three-legged games, or do you stick with track events and the more adventurous sports activities the children use in Secondary School?

Here are some traditional sports dy event ideas:

100m Sprint Race

Use your school running track for one race per year group.

800m Race

Use your school running track for one race per year group.

Relay Race

1 race per year group taking part.

Using your school running track, give your teams a coloured bib and a matching relay baton.

Set out the crossover areas on your school running track.

Discus

Using your school playing field, set out the area safely away from other passing students.

Using a long line tape measure, measure the distance thrown for each pupil taking part.

Shot Put

Using your school playing field, set out the area safely away from other passing students.

Using a long line tape measure, measure the distance thrown for each pupil taking part.

Javelin

Using your school playing field, set out the area safely away from other passing students.

Using a long line tape measure, measure the distance thrown per each pupil taking part.

High Jump

One event per year group

Usually set up as an indoor event with crash mats.

Use your school high jump equipment.

Tug of War

1 team per year group

Teachers Race

Challenge the teachers to a race of their own. Which teacher is fastest, the PE teacher or perhaps a sporty teacher from a different department?

Challenging Games for Everyone

Getting all children involved in the sports dy can be tricky and you usually find that some children in the class are a bit more reserved when it comes to sport.

To make sure they're still active and enjoying the dy, include a few challenging games that aren't quite as 'sporty' but just as competitive and exciting:

Limbo

Pick up a limbo set and set the challenge for the most flexible students.

Reverse Basketball Throw

Challenge your best netball and basketball players that little bit further; set the rules so they must score goals by throwing the ball backwards over their heads!

Football Goal kick

Get the PE teacher in the net and see how many goals you can get passed them; highest score wins.

Table Tennis

Do you have budding table tennis players ready for a challenge?

Traditional primary games of three-legged race and the egg and spoon race are more likely to attract the children less keen on sport as they see this as a more fun event than a typical racing event. By having some of these games included, you have more opportunity for inclusion of the whole school.

The following need to be consider for the sports dy:

- Sun protection against sunburn

- Plenty of water not to dehydrate

- Prevention against heat stroke or heat exhaustion

- Warm up properly

Are you ready for your school sport’s dy? Across the country, children will be lining up hoping to win the 100 metres dash, the sack race or the egg and spoon race. More importantly, many enthusiastic and competitive mums and dads will be hoping to excel in the parents race too.

### Dolphins.doc

Source: `5. LEARNER GUIDE/Grade 8/Datafiles/Chapter 3 Word Data Files/Dolphins.doc`

Legacy Word text transcription. Original visual formatting is not retained.

Dolphins are  HYPERLINK "http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marine_mammal" \o "Marine mammal" marine mammals closely related to  HYPERLINK "http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whale" \o "Whale" whales and  HYPERLINK "http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Porpoise" \o "Porpoise" porpoises. There are almost forty species of dolphin in 17  HYPERLINK "http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genus" \o "Genus" genera. They vary in size from 1.2 m (4 ft) and 40 kg (90 lb) ( HYPERLINK "http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maui%27s_dolphin" \o "Maui's dolphin" Maui's dolphin), up to 9.5 m (30 ft) and 10 tonnes (9.8 long tons; 11 short tons) (the  HYPERLINK "http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Killer_whale" \o "Killer whale" orca or killer whale). They are found worldwide, mostly in the shallower seas of the  HYPERLINK "http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Continental_shelves" \o "Continental shelves" continental shelves, and are carnivores, eating mostly  HYPERLINK "http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fish" \o "Fish" fish and  HYPERLINK "http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Squid" \o "Squid" squid. The  HYPERLINK "http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Family_(biology)" \o "Family (biology)" familie  HYPERLINK "http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oceanic_dolphin" \o "Oceanic dolphin" Delphinidae is the largest in the  HYPERLINK "http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cetacea" \o "Cetacea" Cetacean order, and evolved relatively recently, about ten million years ago, during the  HYPERLINK "http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miocene" \o "Miocene" Miocene. Dolphins are among the most intelligent animals, and their often friendly appearance, an artifact of the "smile" of their mouth line, and seemingly playful attitude have made them very popular in  HYPERLINK "http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_culture" \o "Human culture" human culture.AnatomyDolphins have a streamlined  HYPERLINK "http://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/fusiform" \o "wikt:fusiform" fusiform body, adapted for fast swimming. The tail fin, called the  HYPERLINK "http://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/fluke" \o "wiktionary:fluke" fluke, is used for  HYPERLINK "http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal_locomotion" \o "Animal locomotion" propulsion, while the  HYPERLINK "http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pectoral_fin" \o "Pectoral fin" pectoral fins together with the entire tail section provide directional control. The  HYPERLINK "http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorsal_fin" \o "Dorsal fin" dorsal fin, in those species that have one, provides stability while swimming.The head contains the  HYPERLINK "http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melon_(whale)" \o "Melon (whale)" melon, a round organ used for  HYPERLINK "http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal_echolocation" \o "Animal echolocation" echolocation. In many species, elongated jaws form a distinct beak; species such as the bottlenose have a curved mouth which looks like a fixed smile. Some specy have up to 250 teeth. Dolphins breathe through a  HYPERLINK "http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blowhole_(biology)" \o "Blowhole (biology)" blowhole on top of their head. The  HYPERLINK "http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertebrate_trachea" \o "Vertebrate trachea" trachea is  HYPERLINK "http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anterior" \o "Anterior" anterior to the brain. The  HYPERLINK "http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dolphin_brain" \o "Dolphin brain" dolphin brain is large and highly complex, and is different in structure from that of most land mammals.Unlike most mammals, dolphins do not have hair, except for a few hairs around the tip of their  HYPERLINK "http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rostrum_(anatomy)" \o "Rostrum (anatomy)" rostrum (beak) which they lose shortly before or after birth. The only exception to this is the  HYPERLINK "http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boto" \o "Boto" Boto river dolphin, which has persistent small hairs on the rostrum Dolphins' reproductive organs are located on the underside of the body. Males have two slits, one concealing the  HYPERLINK "http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penis" \o "Penis" penis and one further behind for the  HYPERLINK "http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anus" \o "Anus" anus. The female has one genital slit, housing the  HYPERLINK "http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vagina" \o "Vagina" vagina and the  HYPERLINK "http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anus" \o "Anus" anus. Though the exact methods used to achieve this are not known, dolphins can tolerate and recover from extreme injuries, such as  HYPERLINK "http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shark" \o "Shark" shark bites. The  HYPERLINK "http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Healing" \o "Healing" healing process is rapid and even very deep wounds do not cause dolphins to  HYPERLINK "http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hemorrhage" \o "Hemorrhage" hemorrhage to death. Furthermore, even gaping wounds restore in such a way that the animal's body shape is restored, and  HYPERLINK "http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infection" \o "Infection" infection of such large wounds seems rare. SensesMost dolphins have acute  HYPERLINK "http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eyesight" \o "Eyesight" eyesight, both in and out of the water, and they can hear frequencies ten times or more above the upper limit of adult human hearing. Though they have a small ear opening on each side of their head, it is believed hearing underwater is also, if not exclusively, done with the lower jaw, which conducts sound to the  HYPERLINK "http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middle_ear" \o "Middle ear" middle ear via a fat-filled cavity in the lower jaw bone. Hearing is also used for  HYPERLINK "http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal_echolocation" \o "Animal echolocation" echolocation, which all dolphins have. Dolphin teath are believed to function as antennae to receive incoming sound and to pinpoint the exact location of an object Beyond locating an object, echolocation also provides the animal with an idea on the object's shape and size, though how exactly this works is not yet understood. The  HYPERLINK "http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indus_Dolphin" \o "Indus Dolphin" Indus Dolphin is effectively blind. This may be because not much light penetrates the waters of the  HYPERLINK "http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indus_river" \o "Indus river" Indus river (due to suspended sediments), making eyes futile. The dolphin's sense of touch is also well-developed, with free nerve endings densely packed in the skin, especially around the snout, pectoral fins and genital area. However, dolphins lack an  HYPERLINK "http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olfactory_nerve" \o "Olfactory nerve" olfactory nerve and lobes, and thus are believed to have no  HYPERLINK "http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sense_of_smell" \o "Sense of smell" sense of smell. They do have a sense of  HYPERLINK "http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taste" \o "Taste" taste and show preferences for certain kinds of fish. Since dolphins spend most of their time below the surface, tasting the water could function like smelling, in that substances in the water can signal the presence of objects that are not in the dolphin’s mouth.Though most dolphins do not have hair, they do have  HYPERLINK "http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hair_follicle" \o "Hair follicle" hair follicles that may perform some sensory function The small hairs on the rostrum of the Boto river dolphin are believed to function as a  HYPERLINK "http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Somatosensory_system" \o "Somatosensory system" tactile sense possibly to compensate for the Boto's poor eyesight. HYPERLINK "http://www.dolphins-world.com/Dolphins_and_Humans.html" Dolphins and Humans Humans have been interacting with dolphins for as long as we have known of their existence. In the beginning, human interaction was mainly limited to hunting dolphins. HYPERLINK "http://www.dolphins-world.com/Dolphins_in_Captivity.html" Dolphins in Captivity Learn how dolphins in captivity behave compared with wild dolphins. Stories of boys riding dolphins date all the way back to Roman times, and even today scientific researchers sometimes ride wild dolphins they’re studying. HYPERLINK "http://www.dolphins-world.com/Learning_from_Dolphins.html" Learning from Dolphins While dolphin research is still in its infancy, the wealth of information that we may one day glean from these magnificent creatures is unimaginable. One lesson that we can learn from them today, however, could be a key to the survival of our civilization. HYPERLINK "http://www.dolphins-world.com/Dolphins_in_the_Military.html" Dolphins in the Military Dolphins in the military. We've heard for years that Dolphins are incredibly intelligent creatures. It turns out that they are even intelligent enough to serve in the United States Navy, and have been doing so since 1960. HYPERLINK "http://www.dolphins-world.com/Dolphins_in_Mythology.html" Dolphins in Mythology Dolphins in Mythology. Dolphins have been viewed as somehow magical for millennia by humans. They’re one of the only animals that appear to play, leaping out of the water and doing tricks, and the bottlenose dolphin even seems to grin widely at everything. HYPERLINK "http://www.dolphins-world.com/Dolphins_Rescuing_Humans.html" Dolphins Rescuing Humans Dolphins rescuing and helping humans. Dolphins are social animals, living in groups called pods and taking loving care of their babies. They’re also known to be very friendly to humans. HYPERLINK "http://www.dolphins-world.com/Dolphin_Assisted_Therapy.html" Dolphin Assisted Therapy Dolphin Assisted Therapy. Originating in 1978 by Dr. David Nathanson, Dolphin Assisted Therapy (DAT) has been used as a therapeutic approach to increase speech and motor skills in patients who have been diagnosed with developmental, physical, and/or emotional disabilities, such as mental retardation, Down syndrome, and autism.Dolphin Facts -animalstats- |  |  |  |  | MALE | FEMALE | YOUNG | SOCIAL UIT |  | bull | cow | calf | group |  | GROUP | HOME | HABITAT | FAVOURITE FOOD |  | pod | temperate and tropical oceans | ocean | fish, squid |  | TOP SPEED | LIFESPAN | AVG. LENGTH | AVG.
